decisions.documentation_format: structured configuration and source comments; no Markdown

dependency_direction: domain has no IO or framework dependencies
application depends on domain and ports
feature crates depend on domain and ports
adapters implement ports and own external IO
apps are composition roots and wire concrete adapters
rules: HTTP handlers do not contain business logic
Domain types do not depend on Axum, SQLx, Tokio or HTTP clients
Storage, queue and event implementations are replaceable behind traits
Cross-crate communication uses typed commands, events and errors
No global mutable singleton for runtime state

crates.domain: entities, value objects, domain errors and invariants
crates.application: use cases, orchestration and job lifecycle
crates.ports: repository, queue, proxy, scanner and event traits
crates.config: validated config loading and environment overrides
crates.capture: bounded ingestion, deduplication and flow buffering
crates.storage: SQLite adapter first, PostgreSQL adapter later
crates.workflow: graph model, node registry, execution engine and AI-assisted workflow builder
crates.scanner: replay, fuzz scheduler, rate limits and verification
crates.skills: built-in security skills and skill registry
crates.auth: login flows, token refresh and secret handling
crates.reporting: JSON, HTML, SARIF and Mermaid output
crates.dashboard: versioned API handlers and static asset serving
crates.events: typed in-process events with future external transport
crates.telemetry: structured logs, metrics, traces and health state
crates.test-support: local mock targets, fixtures and deterministic test helpers

production_requirements: Use semantic versioning for binaries, schemas and public APIs
Use forward-only database migrations with startup compatibility checks
Provide health, readiness and liveness endpoints
Use structured logs with request, session and scan-job correlation IDs
Provide metrics for throughput, latency, queue depth, errors and resource usage
Use typed domain errors and avoid panic on user-controlled input
Redact secrets from logs, reports, crash output and telemetry
Pin dependencies and run cargo fmt, clippy, test, audit and deny checks in CI
Produce reproducible release artifacts for Windows MSVC
Keep configuration external to binaries and support environment overrides
Define license, update and rollback behavior before commercial release

scalability_strategy.stage_1: Single modular process with Tokio tasks, bounded channels and SQLite
scalability_strategy.stage_2: Separate API/dashboard from scanner worker while keeping the same application ports
scalability_strategy.stage_3: Replace in-process queue with Redis, NATS or another durable broker
scalability_strategy.stage_4: Move production persistence to PostgreSQL and add horizontally scalable workers
worker_partitioning: partition jobs by scan_id and target scope
make scan jobs idempotent and resumable
scalability_strategy.storage_policy: SQLite for local single-user mode; PostgreSQL through the same repository ports for commercial multi-user mode

event_transport_contract.current: In-process broadcast EventBus; best-effort delivery, lagging receivers drop events without blocking producers
event_transport_contract.ordering: Events are ordered per topic within a single process
event_transport_contract.durability_rule: Flows are persisted by the writer BEFORE the capture event is published; consumers must never treat events as durable storage

scale_out.trigger: When worker processes are split (scale-out stages 2/3), replace the in-process bus with a durable broker behind the existing EventPublisher port
scale_out.guarantees: At-least-once delivery with consumer groups and explicit acknowledgement
scale_out.wire_format: Reuse the serialized DomainEvent as the wire contract; add a schema version field before any external transport lands
scale_out.idempotency: Consumers must tolerate duplicate events, so handler side-effects must be idempotent

workflow_feature.purpose: Post-migration feature to build and run web testing workflows visually or with AI assistance

requirements.logic_builder: Users create workflows through a visual node-based editor: nodes, edges, start and end markers, conditionals and loops
requirements.ai_builder: Users describe a workflow in natural language and the system generates a validated workflow graph
requirements.graph_support: Workflows are directed graphs with explicit node types, edge constraints, input and output schemas
requirements.execution: Workflows run on the Rust engine with per-node input and output state passing and error propagation
requirements.persistence: Workflow definitions and run history are versioned and stored in the same storage layer as flows
requirements.extensibility: New node types register through a static registry without changing the workflow engine

evaluation_criteria: A workflow with at least 10 nodes and 12 edges is created, saved, reloaded and executed end-to-end
Cycle detection rejects invalid graphs before execution and reports the offending edges
Nodes support typed inputs and outputs validated by JSON schema at the graph boundary
Conditional branches and loops produce deterministic results under a fixed seed
Per-node timeout, retry and failure handling are configurable and covered by tests
Natural language prompts produce valid workflow JSON directly or through a bounded repair loop
AI-generated workflows are validated, versioned and executed exactly like logic-built workflows
A workflow run can be cancelled, resumed and replayed with identical results
Workflow-driven requests honor scanner budgets, scope guardrails and rate limits
The visual editor and the AI builder share the same internal graph contract

post_migration_roadmap.name: Workflow builder and engine
goals: Implement the workflow graph model, node registry and execution engine
Build the visual node editor in the dashboard
Add AI-assisted workflow generation behind a provider abstraction
Persist workflow definitions and run history in SQLite
exit_criteria: Graph create, read, update, delete, validation, execution and versioning pass integration tests
AI generation produces schema-valid workflows with bounded repair
Visual editor and AI builder interoperate on the same graph contract
All security guardrails apply to workflow-driven requests

runtime_flow: Rust scanner for replay, fuzzing and brute-force testing

Rust and Python serialization expectations are documented in source/config

phases.name: Storage, buffer and events
goals: Implement SQLite repositories behind the Phase 1 port traits
Implement bounded tokio channels, a dashboard ring buffer and a dedicated persistence writer
Implement deduplication, broadcast events and typed error propagation
Avoid global mutable state and unbounded task creation
Add forward-only migrations and versioned schema checks at startup
exit_criteria: Storage persistence
Flows saved through FlowRepository survive a full process restart and are returned identically
SessionRepository round-trips sessions including end_time and flow_count across restarts
Repository operations are atomic: a failed write leaves no partial row and returns a typed PortError
Concurrent writers to SQLite never deadlock and produce consistent snapshots under a single-writer worker
Large flow bodies (up to the configured cap) persist without truncation and restore byte-for-byte
Buffer and backpressure
A bounded channel rejects or blocks producers when full instead of growing memory without limit
Backpressure is observable: when the persistence writer is slow, buffer occupancy stays bounded and no data is silently lost
Overflow behavior is explicit and configurable (drop-oldest, block, or fail-fast) and covered by tests
The dashboard ring buffer returns a consistent snapshot while producers keep pushing concurrently
Buffer does not allocate unboundedly when producers outpace consumers for a sustained period
Deduplication
Duplicate flows with an identical fingerprint are dropped and counted, and the metric is exposed
Fingerprint collisions with different request bodies are avoided in the tested dataset
Dedup state can be reset without corrupting already-persisted flows
Events
Broadcast events reach all subscribers and a slow subscriber never blocks producers
Events are typed, ordered per topic, and include correlation and session identifiers
Event publishing failures are isolated so one handler failure does not break the pipeline
Migrations and compatibility
Migrations are forward-only and startup fails fast with a clear message on schema mismatch
Existing databases migrate from the current baseline to the latest schema without data loss
Schema includes future-proof tables for workflow graph nodes and edges so Phase 9 requires no destructive change
Concurrency and hygiene
No global mutable singleton is used for runtime state
Task creation is bounded; no unbounded spawn per incoming flow
cargo test --workspace passes with storage and event integration tests
cargo fmt --check passes
cargo clippy --workspace --all-targets -- -D warnings passes
Performance
A benchmark shows sustained flow ingest at the target request rate with bounded memory
Persist latency for a single flow stays within a documented budget at the target concurrency
Memory usage remains flat under sustained ingest and drain cycles

phases.name: Rust proxy
goals: Implement HTTP forwarding and flow capture
Port scope filtering, match/replace and session tracking
Implement CONNECT tunneling and HTTPS MITM
Preserve ports 127.0.0.1:8080 and certificate profile behavior
Implement keep-alive and connection reuse instead of the Python per-request Connection: close behavior
Make body size limits configurable and apply response rewrite rules before relaying to the client
Expose the proxy behind ports (capture sink, session repository) for clean composition
Provide graceful shutdown with in-flight connection drain
exit_criteria: HTTP forwarding and capture
Plain HTTP requests are forwarded and captured end-to-end matching the Python reference behavior
Request and response headers, status line and bodies round-trip without corruption
Multiple sequential requests on one client connection (keep-alive) are each captured correctly
Out-of-scope traffic is forwarded as a blind tunnel and never captured
Request and response bodies are decoded for gzip, deflate and chunked encodings and capped at the configured byte limit
Cookies (names and values) are extracted for request and response without leaking values into logs
HTTPS MITM
CONNECT replies 200 Connection Established and upgrades the connection via TLS
Per-host certificates are generated, cached and signed by the CA; cached certs are reused
CA and host certificates are validated by an integration test against a local TLS upstream
TLS verification or handshake failures produce a clean error path instead of crashing the proxy
Match & replace and scope
Scope include and exclude rules match the Python regex semantics
Match & replace request rules are applied before forwarding to upstream
Response rules are applied before the response is relayed to the client, fixing the Python limitation where rules only touched the captured flow
Session and buffer wiring
Starting the proxy creates a session through SessionRepository and increments flow counts
Captured flows pass through a capture sink into the bounded buffer and event bus
Stopping the proxy closes the active session and drains in-flight connections
Clean architecture
The proxy crate depends only on domain and ports; no sqlx or storage internals leak into it
HTTP parsing and message decoding are isolated pure functions covered by unit tests
cargo test --workspace passes with proxy unit and integration tests
cargo fmt --check passes
cargo clippy --workspace --all-targets -- -D warnings passes
Performance
A benchmark measures plain and HTTPS proxy throughput with keep-alive enabled
Memory stays bounded while streaming large responses up to the configured cap

performance_rules: Use bounded queues and explicit backpressure
Stream or cap large response bodies
Avoid unnecessary request and response copies
Benchmark against local mock targets only
security_guardrails: Enforce scope include and exclude rules before sending mutations
Enforce request, concurrency, duration and payload budgets
Redact credentials and tokens in logs and reports
Do not test targets outside authorized scope
known_risks: HTTPS MITM certificate generation and TLS interception
Header and cookie fidelity during proxy forwarding
Parity differences between Pydantic and serde validation
Workflow graph complexity grows with node types, branching and AI generation quality
MSVC build environment availability on clean machines
The existing pyproject.toml references a deleted README.md and is legacy during migration
